steps.body: Draw that many: same order, pencil edition. Draw circles and count each one as it lands — the numeral says when the pencil stops.
steps.narration: Draw that many: same order, pencil edition. Draw circles and count each one as it lands — the numeral says when the pencil stops.

widget.prompt: Draw-and-count practice: show the 8 your pencil must produce.

commonCounts.feedback: The pencil stopped a circle early; the count must reach eight before resting.
One circle too many landed; counting during the drawing catches it at eight.

widget.missFeedback: One number per circle as you draw; the numeral is the stopping word.
widget.successFeedback: Eight — counted as they landed, stopped on the numeral's word.

predict.prompt: Drawing 5 circles — when do you count them?
predict.reveal: Counting during the drawing stops the pencil on time; counting after finds mistakes too late.

cml.actionGoal: Link the written numeral to the exact amount it names for kcw draw amount.
invariants: A numeral is a written promise about an amount: it records the last word of a careful count, position gives each digit its job, and the promise survives any change of objects or arrangement — the anchor for kcw draw amount.
misconceptions: Treating numerals as decorations, reading digit pairs without position, or matching a numeral to roughly rather than exactly its amount.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more thing joined the group, which single mark of the numeral would have to change?

widget.prompt: Asked to draw 5 circles, when should you stop drawing?

options.label: The moment the count of drawings says 5
options.feedback: Correct — count as you draw; the numeral 5 is the stopping rule.

options.label: When the page is full
options.feedback: The page's size is not the rule; the numeral 5 is.

options.label: After 10, to be safe
options.feedback: Extra circles break the promise — the drawing must match the numeral exactly.

options.label: Never — keep drawing
options.feedback: A drawing that never stops shows no number at all; 5 means stop at five.

hints: Last number said, first mark written.

widget.prompt: What number comes right before 9? Hop one back and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 9 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop back to reach 8.
7 goes one complete hop too far. Count exactly 1 hop back from 9 to reach 8.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 back from 9: you land on 8.
widget.successFeedback: 8 — the numeral written just before 9 names one less.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — one hop back from 9 reaches 8.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right before 9 means a single hop back, stopping on 8.
